chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that whenever he reached the Multazam, he said:

to his mawali, 'Remove me from the crowd so that I may acknowledge my sins to my Lord in this place, for this is a place where a servant does not acknowledge his sins to his Lord and then seek forgiveness, except that Allah forgives him.'

key_terms.أَمِيطُوا عَنِّي: Remove/clear away (from me), instructing others to make space.
key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَم: The Multazam, the section of the Kaaba's wall between the door and the Mihrab, where pilgrims press their chests and foreheads to seek forgiveness.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Multazam and the practice of confessing sins there according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this tradition from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the Multazam as a unique locus for private repentance, instructing his companions to clear the space so he could confess his sins directly to God. This practice underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual potency of the Kaaba's walls, where sincere acknowledgment of wrongdoing is believed to guarantee divine forgiveness, linking physical proximity to the House of God with spiritual purification.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. It was so that whenever he<sup>asws</sup> ended up to Al-Multazam, said to the ones in his<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah: ‘

Go away from me<sup>asws</sup> until I<sup>asws</sup> acknowledge to my<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of my<sup>asws</sup> sins in this place, for this place is such that a servant will not acknowledge his sins to his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, then seek Forgiveness, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, on reaching al-Multazam, would say to his people, ‘
Leave me alone so I can confess to my sins before my Lord at this place; whoever at this place confesses to his sins and thereafter asks Allah to forgive him, Allah forgives his sins.’”
